..
Overall dry conditions have moved into most of the Marianas this 
afternoon, with Guam seeing a few island effect showers linger 
during the mid-afternoon hours. Tinian and Saipan look to remain 
fairly dry over the next several days, and into next week. However, 
with the light winds expected through Tuesday, Saipan has a risk of 
island convection for the next few days. So POPs (Probability of 
Precipitation) were increased to 30 percent for the afternoons at 
Saipan. For Guam, expect increased showers and isolated thunderstorms
to move into the area later tonight, near midnight, as the monsoon 
trough drifts northwest with TS Surigae. This will maintain low-end 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms for Guam through Friday 
night. For Saturday through Tuesday, light and variable winds will 
also maintain the risk of island convection through Tuesday. 
Otherwise, a drier pattern is expected for the remainder of the 
forecast.

Marine...
Benign seas and light to gentle winds will prevail through the
beginning of next week.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Depression Surigae (25W) was upgraded this morning to
Tropical Storm Surigae. TS Surigae is centered west-northwest of 
Saipan near 19.1N 132.5E, moving northwest at 17 mph. Maximum 
sustained winds with Surigae are at 50 mph. Surigae remains in an 
area favorable for development, though it is only expected to 
strengthen slowly over the next few days, possibly becoming a typhoon
sometime over the weekend. Surigae poses no direct threat to the 
Marianas or Micronesia.

For more information on TS Surigae, please refer to bulletins issued
by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and
from the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
The monsoon trough north of Pohnpei has shifted slightly south since
yesterday with the main heavy convection expected to remain north. 
However, scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms will still be 
possible. Gentle to moderate winds will continue through at least 
tomorrow with gustier winds possible with any thunderstorms. Winds 
may decline slightly by the weekend as the monsoon flow breaks apart 
into more individual troughs.

After a brief period of scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms
tonight due to a weak secondary monsoon trough, Kosrae looks to 
remain fairly dry through at least Saturday as it remains south of 
the main trough. Chances for precipitation have increased slightly
for the end of the weekend and into next week with more scattered 
showers and isolated thunderstorms possible. However, model agreement
going into next week is low with some indicating a resurging monsoon
flow and others retaining an extended dry period. Gentle winds 
tonight are expected to become light by Saturday.

Majuro is looking dry with isolated showers through tomorrow before a
new trough moves through Friday night and brings scattered showers 
and isolated thunderstorms. Shower coverage looks to remain scattered
through the rest of the forecast period, possibly increasing by the
middle of next week. Winds will continue decreasing and become light
by tomorrow.

Combined seas of 5 feet tonight will become 4 to 5 feet for all 
islands for most of the forecast period with no significant swells 
expected at this time. Some choppy seas will be possible near heavier
showers and thunderstorms near Pohnpei.

Western Micronesia...
Higher-end scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are expected
to persist at Yap through the forecast period as moist, west to 
southwest flow lingers across the area, before it slowly lifts 
northward over the next couple of days. Locally heavy showers are 
still possible for Yap, but confidence remains low. Mostly isolated 
to low-end scattered showers are expected to continue at Palau 
through Friday before drier conditions settle in this weekend. 
Unsettled weather is expected to develop at Chuuk starting on Friday 
with higher-end scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms forecast
to continue through the weekend and into next week. Gentle to 
moderate west to southwest winds will continue at all sites for the 
next couple of days with winds easing slightly this weekend for Palau
and Yap. Generally benign marine conditions are expected to prevail 
through at least the weekend with combined seas of 3 to 5 feet 
expected at all forecast points. Though, locally choppy seas will be 
possible near Yap with heavier showers and thunderstorms.
